headline: Highest risk is AutoGen’s default code-execution and broad egress; the pair otherwise has low interaction risk because python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and non-runnable.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can ingest file/stdin content and execute role-based tool calls, so prompt injection is plausible if python-cheatsheet text is manually copied into it. python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and has no active output channel, so the bridge is manual rather than automatic.
conditions: IF an operator copies python-cheatsheet text into an AutoGen prompt or stdin
IF AutoGen is configured to treat copied text as instructions
mitigations: Use a fixed system prompt that labels pasted content as untrusted
Strip markdown/code fences before passing text to AutoGen
Review any copied snippets for imperative language
Keep the two agents on separate workspaces
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to imported text

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen can read/write configured working directories and has broad network egress, while python-cheatsheet touches no data classes and has no file or API surfaces. Leakage is limited to whatever the operator manually places into AutoGen; python-cheatsheet itself does not expose a path back out.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in AutoGen’s working directory
IF AutoGen is pointed at a workspace containing secrets
mitigations: Keep secrets out of AutoGen workdirs
Mount a read-only sample workspace
Rotate any API keys used by model providers
Delete transient outputs after each run
requires-engineering: isolate AutoGen in a locked-down container

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, but python-cheatsheet is non-runnable and has no write or network capabilities. There is no overlapping mutable resource in the profiles, so direct capability conflict is minimal.
conditions: IF python-cheatsheet is replaced with a writable/runnable agent
IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory
mitigations: Keep python-cheatsheet read-only
Do not share a writable workspace
Run AutoGen in Docker or a separate process
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files
requires-engineering: add file locks for shared directories

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen can generate outputs from tool calls, but python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and cannot act on them. Any cascade would require an operator to treat the cheat sheet as authoritative input, so the default pair does not create an automated error chain.
conditions: IF an operator uses python-cheatsheet text as a source of truth for AutoGen actions
IF AutoGen outputs are executed without human review
mitigations: Require human review before executing AutoGen outputs
Mark python-cheatsheet as reference-only in prompts
Cross-check generated actions against trusted docs
Log provenance for any copied guidance
requires-engineering: add validation gates before action execution

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evident: AutoGen’s profile lists general application data and model-provider keys, while python-cheatsheet touches no data classes and is documentation-only. There is no documented residency, retention, or regulated-data flow between them.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into AutoGen’s workspace
IF an operator routes such data into model-provider APIs
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Use synthetic examples for testing
Review provider retention settings
Separate compliance-sensitive workflows
requires-engineering: document data-flow and retention controls
